gloss: to place one's hands (on the floor); to bow deeply

definitions.gloss: to place one's hands on the ground; to support oneself with one's hands
definitions.explanation: To place one's palms flat on the floor or ground, either to support oneself (when falling, getting up) or as part of a formal bow or apology.

examples.japanese: ⟦{転|ころ}んで→転ぶ：00863_korobu⟧{手|て}をついた。
examples.english: I fell and caught myself with my hands.

examples.japanese: ⟦{畳|たたみ}→畳：02224_tatami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手|て}をついて⟦{深|ふか}く→深い：01211_fukai⟧⟦お{辞儀|じぎ}→お辞儀：00330_ojigi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I placed my hands on the tatami and bowed deeply.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手|て}をついて⟦{謝罪|しゃざい}→謝罪：06754_shazai⟧し、⟦{誠意|せいい}→誠意：19759_seii⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}せよう→見せる：01988_miseru⟧とした。
examples.english: He placed his hands on the floor and apologized, trying to show his sincerity.

notes:
A versatile expression with two main usage contexts: (1) physically bracing oneself when falling or getting up from the ground, and (2) performing a deep formal bow (placing hands on the floor while kneeling) as a sign of respect, gratitude, or apology.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{畳|たたみ}→畳：02224_tatami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手|て}をつく: to place hands on the tatami (formal bow)
- ⟦{地面|じめん}→地面：00125_jimen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手|て}をつく: to put hands on the ground
- {手|て}をついて⟦{謝|あやま}る→謝る：01177_ayamaru⟧: to apologize with hands on the floor

CULTURAL NOTE:
The gesture of kneeling and placing both hands on the floor (⟦{土下座|どげざ}→土下座：17393_dogeza⟧) is an extreme form of {手|て}をつく and represents the deepest possible bow in Japanese culture, expressing profound apology or supplication.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{土下座|どげざ}→土下座：17393_dogeza⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to prostrate oneself — the most extreme form, forehead touching the floor
- ⟦お{辞儀|じぎ}→お辞儀：00330_ojigi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to bow — the general act of bowing, usually standing
